A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Fourier Learning Machines study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original PDE approximation experiments, optimal-control simulations and hyperparameter-search results in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains those results and adds original Burgers’ equation, five-strategy optimal-control and ETTh1 imputation experiments. Its imputation baseline scores are separately attributed to prior work.

M1.justification: The cosine-activated subnetworks, shared sign-flipped frequencies, trainable amplitudes and phases, initialization and output construction remain unchanged. The additional applications instantiate the existing architecture rather than introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: V2 adds discontinuous inviscid Burgers’ solutions, a five-strategy extension of the optimal-control problem, and univariate ETTh1 oil-temperature imputation with 10% and 50% missingness. These substantially extend the smooth-PDE and three-strategy coverage retained from v1.

E2.justification: Appendix B, Table 3 introduces comparisons with MRNN, SAITS, AutoFormer, Mean and Median, using scores attributed to Du et al. (2024). This adds a distinct comparator family; membership in the retained PDE comparisons is unchanged. New baseline runs are not established.

E3.justification: New protocols include chronological 60/20/20 splitting, normalization and masking for ETTh1; a Godunov reference for Burgers; and specified network sizes and initial-condition sampling for five-strategy control. The fixed-initial-condition experiment also changes its reported Adam beta1 from 0.99 to 0.9, without establishing a rerun. Existing PDE selection procedures are largely relocated to Appendix C.

E4.justification: Figure 9 adds a controlled capacity study spanning subnet counts from 1 to 196 across four PDEs, extending substantially beyond v1’s small tuning grids. The five-strategy experiment explicitly examines scalability, while Burgers supplies a discontinuous-solution stress case.

E5.justification: Ten-seed mean/standard-deviation reporting and the Shapiro–Wilk, ANOVA/Tukey or Friedman/Nemenyi selection procedure are retained. The new result tables extend this reporting practice without establishing increased run counts or a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Original PDE summary values, Tables 5–20 and original result plots are unchanged. New results include Burgers MSE of 6.55e-3 for FLM versus 4.58e-3 for V Tan, five-strategy control MAPE of 0.67%, and ETTh1 MAEs of 0.57 ± 0.15 and 0.66 ± 0.18 at 10% and 50% missingness. Capacity curves and Burgers tuning results are also added; these are new evaluations, not gains on retained settings.

T1.justification: The Fourier representations, coefficient relationships, architectural definitions and Appendix A derivation remain mathematically equivalent. S becoming S(m), the additional two-dimensional matrix example and equilibrium-variable renaming do not change the theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims of a complete separable multidimensional Fourier representation in an MLP-like architecture and accuracy comparable to or often exceeding established networks. Rewording and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly notes exponential neuron growth with input dimension and qualifies PDE superiority with the Burgers exception, attributing difficulty to discontinuity. Appendix B acknowledges preliminary, non-superior imputation performance and reported ranks of 26/29 and 24/29. Future-work discussion also shifts toward high-frequency initialization and Gaussian-process connections.

D1.justification: V2 adds parameter-count formulas and counts in Table 4, ETTh1 preprocessing and training instructions, and architecture/optimizer details for five-strategy control. Original initialization and tuning grids remain documented. Appendix C introduces an ambiguous '1827' configuration count where v1 specifies '18–27', despite retaining the original tables.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a substantive comparison with sparse spectral Gaussian processes, citing Lázaro-Gredilla, Neal and Murphy. The imputation appendix adds dataset, benchmark and comparator references. The existing Fourier-network literature review and central novelty positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording and notation edits, revises author-contribution footnotes, adopts author–year citations and expands architectural explanations. Hyperparameter-selection prose moves from Section 5.1 to Appendix C, and future-work paragraphs are revised; the main narrative and section order remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reformats the document, combines v1’s PDE tables into Table 2 panels and its solution plots into Figure 5, and adds Burgers panels. It also adds a three-input architecture diagram, imputation and parameter-count tables, capacity plots and Burgers tuning tables. Retained plots are reused, while appendix tables are more densely arranged.

improvement.justification: The new discontinuous-PDE, five-strategy and real-data tests better probe the scope of v1’s evidence, while capacity analysis and explicit accuracy/scalability qualifications improve transparency. These gains are tempered by the preliminary imputation comparison using borrowed baseline scores, the ambiguous configuration count, and retained blanket superiority wording despite the Burgers exception. The net improvement is useful but limited.
